name: Lugungu
catalog_citation: Casali, Rod & Martin Diprose (2007). Lugungu Phonology Statement. Issue B, approved June 28, 2007. SIL International, Uganda-Tanzania Branch. 110 pp. PDF from https://www.webonary.org/lugungu/files/…
catalog_locator: sec. 11 Tone, p. 58 (also 11.1 Lexical Tone p. 58; 11.5.2 p. 60-61); whole-document search for 'stress'/'accent' = 0 hits
catalog_quote: Lugungu is typical of many Bantu languages in that it exhibits a rich tonal system. Unfortunately the Phonetic Analysis Worksheet upon which this Statement is based did not examine the tonal system. However, some analysis has been done and it has been summarised and added to this Phonology Statement in this section. Lugungu is analysed as having an underlying two tone distinction, although tonal processes result in a surface distinction between high, low, rising, and falling. In addition there is unconditioned downstep resulting from floating low tones. Tone is utilised to distinguish words, indicate grammatical categories, and indicate grammatical relationships ... 11.1 Lexical Tone A number of words are identical except for tone. ... While lexical tone is clearly present, the number of contrasts where lexical tone alone is the distinguishing factor are relatively few in Lugungu. ... 1…

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim in the held born-digital SIL PDF at the stated section/pages (sec. 11 p. 58; 11.5.2 p. 60), and the '0 hits for stress/accent' locator claim re-verified on the text layer. (2) The deciding source is a 110-pp SIL phonology statement (2007) co-authored by Rod Casali; Glottolog (local 5.1 bib and live query, 8 refs) and OLAC list no grammar, sketch, dissertation or other phonology for Gungu, so it is the best available description and we hold it. (3) Two further open Lugungu documents were fetched sources now: the 2008 Orthography Guide independently states 'Lugungu is a tonal language' with lexical and tense tone contrasts and never mentions stress (confirms); the 2011/2012 dictionary is silent. The only conceivable upgrade is the unpublished SIL tone analysis both documents allude to, which I cannot locate in any catalogue (access unknown, low priority). Caveat on sear

sources.quote: 'Lugungu is a tonal language. Tone is the pitch melody that overlies all words in the language. This pitch melody gives the hearer part of the meaning of words. Two words that are written the same can have two different meanings if they are spoken with different tone melodies.' ... 'Extensive analysis of the tone system in Lugungu has been carried out.
